reflection.text:
This was a blinded MOA run unblinded as proteasome inhibitor I (PubChem CID 16760625, name and BBBC021 structure agree, no ChEMBL curated mechanism) - truth Protein degradation - and both the agent call (p=0.62) and protocol (4/4 wells, 1-NN majority vote) were correct. I was the Scientist in this run.

What the evidence got right was the early and unanimous atlas comparison. After e2 (10 uM, w_d128269dd7: tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean +11.3, tub_std +9.7) and e3 (0.3 uM, w_ad5942f01b: tub_mean +7.6, nuc_dna_mean -6.3, nuc_dna_integrated +5.8), e4 already showed NSC 2/2 Protein degradation. That held to e8 after e6 (1 uM, w_0e5c8b0c20: nuc_eccentricity +11.8, nuc_dna_mean -7.6, nuc_dna_integrated +4.9) and e7 (0.03 uM, w_b1465a0435: tub_mean +7.2, nuc_dna_integrated +6.8, nuc_dna_mean -6.0) - NSC 4/4 with similarities 0.496 to 0.603 across a 300-fold concentration range. The strongest similarity was actually at the lowest acquired dose (0.03 uM, 0.603), which correctly told me the signature was already saturated.

The consistent nuclear pairing - increased integrated DNA with decreased mean DNA intensity plus increased eccentricity - across e3, e6, e7 was what, with hindsight, distinguishes proteostasis arrest from direct microtubule action. That pattern of large, pale nuclei is consistent with proteasome inhibition driving G2-M and broader proliferative arrest as reported for PS-341 and MG-132 class inhibitors PMID 12631620 PMID 19557642 PMID 18638451, rather than a mitotic spindle artifact. The review critique notes this was further supported quantitatively by decreased mitotic fraction vs. visual impression, which is why I kept Protein degradation at 0.58 in e12 despite the visual conflict.

What misled me - or nearly did - was the tubulin channel. e2, e3, e6, e7 all show markedly elevated tub_mean (z +7.2 to +11.3) with extreme texture contrast at 10 uM, and e5 describe_phenotype on 4 fields explicitly called Microtubule stabilizers candidate with lower density. Morphological profilers can recover proteasome-related states PMID 38837838 PMID 38576795 but a secondary tubulin bundling phenotype after proteasome arrest can mimic stabilizers visually. That is why I retained Microtubule stabilizers at 0.32 in e12; the k-neighbour distribution in e8 (Protein synthesis 4/10, Protein degradation 3/10, DNA damage 1/10) also showed near-neighbour ambiguity even as NSC was unanimous.

My acquisition choices both helped and limited interpretation. list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.003-10 uM with 4 wells budget, and I sampled 10, 0.3, 1, and 0.03 uM (all rep 1). That spanning strategy was correct to show dose-persistence - the full tubulin + large-nucleus signature was present even at 0.03 uM - but it meant I had only n=4 for dose_response (e9 rho +0.40 p=0.6 for tub_mean; e10 rho -0.80 p=0.2 for nuc_dna_integrated; e11 rho -0.80 p=0.2 for cell_count). With saturation at the low end and no replicates, I could not demonstrate monotonic dose-dependence and incorrectly interpreted flat trends as weak evidence. I missed the opportunity to sample 0.003-0.01 uM to find the true onset threshold, and to acquire replicate wells to tighten p-values. Budget was exhausted to 0/4, but as the review noted the unanimous NSC vote made an additional acquisition unnecessary for the protocol call.

The literature search after unblinding correctly returned 0 hits for the exact PSI queries (e16, e17) and only broad MG132 signal (e18: 18 hits, 5 returned), so I cannot cite a paper for direct PSI-induced tubulin bundling and make that claim without citation. The general principle that proteasome inhibitor profiling classifies by morphology PMID 38837838 PMID 38576795 and that PS-341/MG-132 arrest involves G2-M PMID 12631620 is supported.

In sum: I relied on e4/e8 NSC over e5 visual, calibrated to p=0.62, and submitted the correct Protein degradation conclusion. The miss was over-weighting tub_mean magnitude as evidence for direct microtubule action before checking the nuclear DNA mean vs integrated dissociation and the lack of true mitotic enrichment across all four acquired well(s). Future real-lab test I proposed remains appropriate: compare a reference proteasome inhibitor vs reference microtubule stabilizer for proteasome activity/ubiquitin conjugates, tubulin polymerization, and phospho-H3 mitotic index. No clinical advice is implied; this is screening morphology data only.
